messages:
maria: Heads-up — on prod long-chat workloads we're seeing sustained heap growth over 6+ hour sessions. Not a leak in app logic; traces point at KV cache fragmentation (lots of tiny KV allocations + large slab class).

dan: yup saw that in the dashboard this morning, mem-usage climbs slowly then plateaus at +18% on some hosts.

maria: attaching quick repro notes: repeated long-context generation (50k tokens) with many short prefix updates causes allocation churn. KV slab internal usage drops to ~55% (lots of 4KB holes).

kevin: ran a profiler on a repro node. (/sys tooling)
```
$ ./kvprof --dump-slab-stats --top=20
slab_class  size   used_pct  free_chunks  total_chunks
4KB         4096   54%       11234        20123
64KB        65536  79%       120          575
256B        256    12%       9800         11200

fragmentation_score: 0.38
hot_entry_count: 1843
cold_entry_evicted: 72/min
```
kevin: TLDR: a lot of small entries mixed with occasional big KV causes many partially used 4KB pages; allocator isn't coalescing well.

anna: Thoughts: either introduce smaller allocation bins for small KV (32/128/512) or aggressive background compaction that relocates cold small entries into dense pages and frees large holes.

rahul: background compaction worked before but caused latency spikes. Need to define CPU budget + safe windows. Also we should avoid moving hot entries — that invalidates pointer lifetimes and can bump p95.

maria: agreed. did a micro-experiment: enabled compaction on one node with a 5% CPU cap; memory dropped ~11% after 30min but we saw a ~8ms p95 spike during compaction windows.

kevin: raw numbers from the canary:
- baseline mem: 11.8GB
- compaction on node: 10.5GB after warmup (-11%)
- observed brief CPU bursts up to +18% but avg CPU within 5% budget
- p95 latency: baseline 42ms -> 50ms during compaction windows

dan: Not great for latency-sensitive customers. Alternative: change allocator bin sizes so small KV don't live in 4KB pages at all. Should reduce internal fragmentation without moving objects.

anna: here's a proto config for a hybrid approach (small bin + gentle compaction):
```yaml
kv_allocator:
  bins: [32, 128, 512, 4096, 65536]
  prefetch_per_bin: 64
compactor:
  enabled: true
  cpu_budget_pct: 3
  min_free_ratio: 0.25  # run when fragmentation > 25%
  move_cold_after_tokens: 10000
  backoff_ms: 200
```

rahul: +1 to move_cold_after_tokens; that avoids thrashing active contexts. Also add trace spans around compaction so we can correlate p95 spikes with compaction windows.

maria: action items:
- @kevin run a throughput bench for new bin config (32/128/512) on 10% canary (estimate mem gains, no compaction).
- @anna prototype compactor with cpu cap & trace spans.
- @dan add allocator unit tests for object migration and pointer stability.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: kv-allocator-bin-change -> canary group (10%) by maria. ETA 8m.

kevin: quick note from bench run (local VM, synthetic): switching bins reduced 4KB slab used_pct from 54% -> 82% (effective densification), total mem -9%. No compaction needed. CPU cost negligible.

maria: cool. let's run those benches on real canaries. prioritize low-latency traffic path keep p95 < +10ms.

dan: also let's add a fragmentation gauge to dashboards: slab_free_ratio and compaction_inflight. Need alert if fragment_score > 0.35 for >15m.

maria: agreed. I'll own the canary and post follow-up with metrics after 24h. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
